description: Solo developer working on AI and web development solution for this challenge.
summary: SpaceMed is an autonomous onboard health monitoring and medical decision-support platform designed for long-duration deep-space missions where communication latency prevents real-time Earth medical intervention. Combining multi-vital biometric telemetry, deterministic threshold anomaly detection, and an AI Flight Surgeon assistant, SpaceMed tracks 864+ physiological and environmental readings across crew profiles—including Heart Rate, SpO2, Cabin Pressure, Ionizing Radiation Dose (mSv), Neurological Stress Index, and Core Temperature. Its dual-layer engine runs instant local Z-score and threshold rules for zero-latency CRITICAL and WARNING alerts (such as Solar Particle Events or EVA stress surges) while providing astronauts with step-by-step, NASA-aligned medical protocols even when offline.
details:
SpaceMed solves the critical challenge of autonomous crew healthcare during lunar and Martian missions where 4 to 24-minute one-way signal delays make real-time ground flight-surgeon support impossible.

How It Works & Technical Architecture:

  1. Synthetic Biometric Telemetry Pipeline (Python / NumPy / SciPy): Generates 864 synchronized 5-minute telemetry frames across 3 crew profiles over 24 hours, modeling microgravity baselines and injected spaceflight hazards (Solar Particle Events > 0.50 mSv, EVA Stress Surges, and Cabin Hypoxia Precursors).
  2. Deterministic Local Triage Engine (Next.js 16 / TypeScript): Computes rolling prior-window Z-scores and strict physiological thresholds on the server (/api/triage) to trigger instant NOMINAL, WARNING, or CRITICAL urgency levels with zero external network dependency.
  3. Onboard AI Medical Decision Support: Integrates Large Language Models (Google Gemini / OpenAI SDKs) to explain anomaly findings and guide astronauts through structured NASA-inspired action checklists, while local safety rules strictly retain control over critical alerts.
  4. Interactive Mission Console (React / Tailwind CSS / Recharts): Features crew switching, 2-hour sparkline vital cards, a 24-hour multi-axis telemetry replay scrubber, hazard event jumps, and frame export capabilities.

Intended Impact: SpaceMed enhances astronaut autonomy and crew safety for Artemis Lunar Gateway and Mars transit habitats, with direct terrestrial applications for remote telemedicine in submarines, polar stations, and disaster-response zones.
